coachingPoints: Track "extra pass" possessions on film and praise them publicly — behavior that gets celebrated gets repeated.
Drill advantage maintenance with 4v3 continuous play: the offense must score without letting the defense recover.
Teach spacing discipline — standing too close together kills advantages faster than any defense.
The extra pass is a skill: practice throwing it on the move, off the catch, under control.
commonMistakes: Catching the kick-out pass and holding the ball, letting the defense reset.
Settling for a contested shot while an advantage is available one pass away.
Drifting inside the three-point line and shrinking the floor for everyone.
Over-passing: turning a good shot into a turnover by forcing one pass too many.
description: Creating an advantage is only half the job. Learn how to keep it alive — extra pass, re-attack, and spacing — until the defense breaks.
gameSituations: Drive-and-kick: the extra pass swings around the perimeter to the open corner.
Short roll: the roller catches in a 4-on-3 and finds the next open man.
Transition: the trailer keeps the break alive with a quick swing instead of stopping the ball.

howTo.detail: When you catch the ball with an advantage and the defense is still rotating, pass to the next open man instead of settling. One more pass often turns a good shot into a great one.
howTo.title: Make the extra pass

howTo.detail: Catch on the move and drive straight at the recovering defender. Never let a rotating defender get set — attack the rotation before it lands.
howTo.title: Re-attack the rotation

howTo.detail: Stay wide and behind the three-point line so the defense has maximum ground to cover. Players who drift inside make rotations short and easy.
howTo.title: Hold your spacing

howTo.detail: Catch, read, and act in under two seconds. The ball must move faster than defenders can run — every extra dribble is a gift to the defense.
howTo.title: Keep the ball moving with quick decisions

howTo.detail: If the defense has fully recovered and matched up, the advantage is gone. Reset the offense and create a new one instead of forcing a bad shot.
howTo.title: Recognize when the advantage is dead

howTo.detail: The last pass should produce the highest-value shot available: a layup first, then an open three, then everything else. Finish the chain with discipline.
howTo.title: Finish the chain

title: Maintaining Advantages
whatIsIt: Maintaining an advantage means keeping the defense in rotation after you have broken it down. You beat your man and the help comes — now what? If you stop, the defense recovers and the advantage dies. If you keep the ball moving or re-attack the next defender, the advantage grows until someone is wide open.

The tools of maintenance are simple: the extra pass, the quick re-drive, and holding your spacing so the defense cannot recover. Great offensive teams do not just create one advantage per possession — they chain them: advantage, rotation, re-attack, open shot.
whyItMatters: Most wasted possessions are not wasted because no advantage was created — they are wasted because the advantage was created and then given back. A kick-out to a player who holds the ball lets the defense reset for free. Maintaining advantages is what separates good offenses from great ones.
It is also a trust builder. Players who make the extra pass earn their teammates' trust, and trusted teams share the ball willingly. The extra pass is both a tactic and a culture.
